worked: Single, 50, wages 160,000: Wisconsin income at or over 155,169, so the table gives 0 standard deduction. Taxable income is 100,000 or more, so the form uses the Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 44, Section A: x 5.3% less 586.44). Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 160,000.00 = 160,000.00. Federal taxable income = 160,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 144,250.00; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Form 1 line 1 federal AGI 160,000.00; line 2 Schedule I adjustments 0.00; line 3 160,000.00; line 4 additions 0.00; line 5 160,000.00. Schedule SB: no subtraction applies; line 50 0.00. Form 1 line 6 0.00; line 7 Wisconsin income = 160,000.00 - 0.00 = 160,000.00. Line 8 standard deduction, 2025 Standard Deduction Table (Form 1 Instructions PDF page 37), row 155,169 or more, column Single: 0.00 (printed row, at least / less than / single / joint / separate / head of household: 155,169 or more / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0). Line 9 = 160,000.00 - 0.00 = 160,000.00. Line 10a 1 x 700 = 700.00; line 10b 0 x 250 = 0.00; line 10c 700.00. Line 11 taxable income = 160,000.00 - 700.00 = 159,300.00. Line 12 tax, Schedule A (single) as numbers: 3.5% x 14,680.00 = 513.80 + 4.4% x 35,800.00 = 1,575.20 + 5.3% x 108,820.00 = 5,767.46; total 7,856.46, rounded once to 7,856.46. The Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 44) gives the same before its whole-dollar entry. Credits (lines 13-20, 30-35): none modelled; 0.00. State income tax 7,856.46.
